problem: All snapshot delete buttons were disabled when only terminal failed recovery history remained
cause: SystemRecoveryPanel emitted attentionCount including failed jobs. SystemSnapshotsPanel interpreted that count as an unresolved recovery blocker, even though the recovery status was ready and the backend allowed deletion.
fix: attentionCount now includes only attention_required; queued/running remain active blockers. Failed history stays visible in the recovery table and no longer blocks deletion.
protected_semantics: Excluded from automatic retention cleanup; may still be permanently deleted manually after explicit consent. Badge hover and deletion dialog explain the meaning.

red_test.failure: Expected attentionCount=0 but received 4 for four historical failed jobs and one completed job

new_browser_cases: Desktop and narrow screens with four failed and one completed recovery history entry
All protected, ready and failed snapshots deletable after confirmation
Queued/running/attention_required events disable deletion; terminal failed history re-enables through SSE
Protected deletion sends explicit true; ordinary and failed deletion send false
validation.visual_inspection: desktop and narrow protected deletion dialogs inspected

scope: Frontend status classification and explanation only. No backend deletion authorization or physical-cleanup logic changed; the prior native deletion report remains separate.
rollout: Refresh the current development backup page; published deployments require the updated Web Admin bundle. No Core restart is required for this follow-up.
limits: Browser deletion endpoints were controlled fixtures; this follow-up did not delete live user snapshots or repeat native backend acceptance.
